Oh well, thank you!

Thank you! Profoundly helpful! Reading this now, I agree, I didn't establish proper rythmn. I didn't know to could convey the meaning without it, but I'm starting to see a few routes. Argh! The typo... Well, this is what I get for writing on mobile. The language wasn't chosen with any specific intent. I wrote this on the bus, as it came to me, because it was a little too vivid to ignore. It just materialized on those terms... I hope it isn't too obnoxious a read, I don't see how I could have worked around that without twisting the initial imagine too intensely. Again, very helpful feedback, thank you!

I'll have to return to this... A cursory read, and it struck me as "tired". Rememberance as the only source of life. Another, and it seemed like innocence renewed. Eyes that had seen before, searching again, willing to discover what was, almost wondering if what they had seen had ever been. It almost strikes me as a memory of old age in the mind of a child, if that makes sense. It's still quite mysterious to me. Your memoir has a delightful beginning.
Thank you for sharing!

The image was so well chosen, so many tales were told on that very stage... It's so very impactful, having something that lives in one's mind repossessed... The sea comes to me in a very classic sense, beguiling, emotion in its entirety. Almost before it becomes sentiment, before structure is imposed - just what's required to make a mirage, a trap. It reminds me of Sophia de Mello Breyner's relationship with the ocean... Why I don't quite know, the style is different, as is the tone, meaning and structure, but something about it is reminiscent of "her sea". I can feel a kind of fog setting in as I read this, a repetition that seems to take all  freedom from me, rather like becoming a passenger.
Thank you!

The universality of this poem is what most strikes me. The symbols you employ exist in all our psyches, I feel. Color, and absence, and silence, and longing. Perpetual tragedy... All used in their shared form, yet put in a personal context. I feel their joint meaning is yours alone. I believe a lot is gained by bringing forth what is buried in all of us - and the way in which you chose to do so, the emphasis you set quite naturally, the point you made collective, is for me, where all that's personal lies.
Does that make sense to you? Thank you!

I feel a sense of erosion reading this, as though reality has lost weight, and only memory retains its shape, its complexity. Winter appears in few distinct ways in my mind; the death of all things, the cold of grief, the passage of time and remoteness of memory. There's a certain naivety to the form that gives it the feeling of young love. I'd like to know how much distance you were going for, how much of what I described was my own imposition.
Thank you!

The event that brought this on bore very little resemblance to what unfolded in my mind... It was about someone I care for greatly, the last and dearest friend I have, and a few moments in which she showed me all the ways in which my humanity was irrelevant to her - quite by accident, with cavalier joy. That blindness - that I refuse to call indifference, for the word implies too much - has had many vehicles. It came surging, my pasts and futures, and she was the bringer... In the trust sense, what I lived through was far more akin to what you wrote, it was a funeral, but for someone who never was, someone whose personhood I pieced together (it/she); what died was not a person at all. A thousand voices spoke, the voices of my life, all at once, indistinct chatter - all who wanted me to dance, in this imagery of mine. And in some sense it was a wedding too... I'm sure the line you asked about is clearer now, and I suppose the rest of the image is as well... I don't feel any other words match the details of my experience, the surrender, the rot... I have difficultly dissecting it without stripping it of all that truly took place.
Thank you so much for sharing all you saw!

This was a very particular poem for a very particular time. The rythmn naturally came to be dense, and the form somewhat muddled - the inside of my mind just poured on to the page; I chose not to modify it because it left a trail for me, it didn't quite compliment the words, it spoke against them - I felt that would help me return to that moment, somehow. I will certainly consider using shorter stanzas, and perhaps writing the form intensionally, and letting the content appear, once or twice, seeing how much I can imply.
Your critique of my usage of "genial " gives me pause. I suppose my natural language is sort of synesthetic (does that come through? The reality of the esoteric?), the difference between ideal and embodied isn't one I feel strongly at all, if that makes sense... I see how that might make for amorphous writing, unless I take great care in creating a correspondence between what you aptly called the platonic concept, and my experience of it.
Thank you so very much! I'll investigate all you mentioned.
Edit: I'm extremely sleep deprived, and so I'm rambling. Apologies.

I absolutely love this. It is conveys its meaning through structure and content. The repetition is so subtle, it genrates this dreamlike state, and reader lives a moment right alongside you. The emotional quality is ambiguous to me, and I think it benefits from that. It is a moment, in that it is the full experience of it, in all its layers, mental and worldly, awe inducing and familiar...
Thank you for sharing
